title: How to Vet an AI Ad Agency
summary: An AI advertising agency should own a clear creative or media scope. Compare human review, rights, delivery and reporting instead of relying on AI claims.
body_markdown:
## What should an AI agency demonstrate in a paid pilot?


Commission a pilot that resembles the work you expect to repeat. A spectacular scene unrelated to your product tells you little about the supplier's ability to maintain accurate packaging, handle feedback or deliver usable variants. Choose one ordinary production requirement and one difficult requirement, then agree the acceptance criteria before the team starts.


For an illustrative home-coffee product, the ordinary requirement might be a presenter explaining the approved offer. The difficult requirement might be a close-up of the machine dispensing coffee. Supply reference photos and authentic footage of the mechanism. Ask the agency to recommend which material to generate, which to retain and how the two will be edited together. You are buying a production judgment as well as an output.


Review the pilot at three points. At concept approval, check whether the message answers a customer question. At the rough cut, check whether the proof supports that message and the product behaves correctly. At delivery, check every promised export and its destination. Record the changes your team requested and the decisions the supplier made without prompting.


The pilot's result should be a decision about the working arrangement: continue the approach, revise the method or choose a different supplier. Campaign performance is a separate question that needs its own observation conditions. A production pilot can establish whether the workflow is usable without establishing which ad will sell best.


## How do you evaluate the human work behind automation?


Ask for a practical division of labor. “Human in the loop” is incomplete until you know who can reject a script, correct a product detail and approve a campaign change. Map those decisions to roles rather than requesting a list of every software tool the agency uses.


A useful review artifact is an annotated rough cut. Each note should identify the issue, the required correction and the reason. “The lid opens from the wrong side” is actionable. “Make it more premium” needs a reference or a more specific direction. Ask the agency to show how it turns ambiguous feedback into an agreed revision before spending another production cycle.


Also examine exceptions. Suppose an approved presenter is consistent in a wide shot but changes appearance in a close-up. The team should explain whether it would regenerate the scene, change the framing, use an approved still or rewrite the sequence. The important evidence is the reasoning and whether the chosen fix preserves the message. A longer software list does not resolve that decision.


In an end-to-end Meta engagement, extend the responsibility map beyond delivery: who connects the approved asset to the intended campaign, who authorizes spending and who brings campaign findings into the next brief? Knowlify can own creative and campaign management together. Your agreement should specify those responsibilities and the private service fee, with media spend separate.


## How can you compare AI proposals without counting unusable output?


Create an acceptance ledger for the pilot. Give each planned ad an identifier and record its status: awaiting inputs, awaiting review, approved, requires correction or removed from scope. Keep drafts and technical exports visible without treating them as new concepts. This makes disagreements about a headline output allowance easier to resolve.


Consider an illustrative quote offering twelve finished ads. If the plan contains three messages with four hooks each, record three concepts and twelve variants. If one message depends on an unsupported product claim, the relevant question is how that concept will be replaced, not whether the supplier can generate its files quickly. Define the handling of rejected concepts in the agreement.


Compare the complete working cost using your own assumptions. Include the service fee, any separately required tools, agreed rights costs and internal review time. Keep media spend on its own line. Do not label unused creative as a saving merely because its nominal cost per export is low. Equally, do not assume an expensive polished asset is a better purchase without considering where and how it will be used.


## What belongs in the next production brief?


End each review by carrying forward specific decisions. Record which product facts are fixed, which visual treatment passed review, what the campaign team observed and what question remains open. Avoid a vague instruction to generate more of the same.


For the coffee example, the next brief could preserve the approved machine footage while testing a morning-routine message against an entertaining-guests message. Keep the offer and product behavior accurate in both. If the campaign evidence is inconclusive, say so and explain why the next brief is still worth producing. This creates a documented learning process without turning every observation into a claim of causation.


Knowlify's creative-only option can use the same process with your existing buyer. Ask that buyer to supply a short decision note with the next request so the production team understands the commercial question, not merely the desired style.

## Key takeaways


- Compare responsibilities and outputs, not an AI label.
- Inspect an ordinary project and a difficult revision.
- Review permissions, identity and labeling separately.
- Use the[total-cost guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/diy-ai-video-ads-vs-done-for-you) to include internal work.


## FAQ


### Is an AI agency the same as an ad generator?


An ad generator supplies software access. An agency proposal should identify the people responsible for concepts, scripts, production, review and any campaign work you are purchasing. Ask for an ordinary project walkthrough and a complete delivery example. Compare the work transferred and the work retained by your team, not only the available tools.


### Does AI guarantee faster production?


This guide makes no universal turnaround claim. Ask for a delivery schedule based on your brief, supplied assets and approval requirements, and test the difficult scenes before expanding the batch.


### Can AI-made ads use real brand products?


Provide authorized, accurate product assets and require final review against them. Confirm that generated scenes do not alter features, packaging or the impression of how the product works.


### What should remain under client control?


Keep approved claims, brand rules, budget authority and final acceptance clearly assigned to your team. Document reporting access and the handover of files and permissions when the engagement ends.
